title: Private Deploy Intake: Customer-driven Network Change Windows & Airgap Upgrade Orchestration
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Problem: Enterprise customers frequently submit private/VPC/on-prem upgrade requests that are constrained by narrow network change windows, bespoke upgrade scripts, and strict airgap rules. Current intake and prioritization treats these as generic 'network' requests which misses the operational risk (rollback complexity, manual operator time) and causes missed SLA commitments. Goal: evolve intake, scoring, and playbooks to explicitly capture 'network-change-window' constraints and 'customer-run upgrade scripts' as first-class triage signals; add a fast-lane for low-risk preflightable upgrades and a staged manual lane for high-risk bespoke upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated: new fields for network_change_window (timezone, start/end UTC), customer_upgrade_script (yes/no + artifact link), and airgap_classification (full/partial/none) available in self-serve and sales intake templates.

Triage rubric updated and documented: weight matrix includes change_window_risk, automation_coverage, rollback_complexity, and dependency_surface. Rubric pilot run on 20 historical requests with score drift <= 10% vs manual PM decisions.

Fast-lane defined: preflight probe + sandbox run checklist that reduces human ops touch for scores <= 25 and customer_impact != high. At least one customer onboarded via fast-lane in pilot by due_date.
Manual lane playbook: operator-run upgrade runbook, mandatory snapshot and rollback confirmation, and escalation path to eng + security for scripts altering networking or cluster config.
Confluence PRD and runbooks linked and reviewed by Security & Solutions Eng (review comments resolved).
Dashboard tile (Console -> Private Onboarding) shows intake counts by change_window_bucket and lane assignment within 1 week of rollout.
Automation stub (preflight probe) prototype committed as feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/private-onprem-preflight #PR-1842 exists and is linked.
comments: 2025-01-10 Aisha Banerjee: Created ticket after Sales flagged 3 missed SLAs in Dec 2024 tied to narrow 2-hour change windows and custom upgrade scripts. Noted repeated operational toil and late-night oncalls.

2025-01-14 Marco Ruiz: Scoped initial intake form fields. Proposed fields: change_window_start_utc, change_window_end_utc, contact_timezone, upgrade_script_link, script_owner, requires_inbound_ports, egress_exemptions, airgap_classification. Shared draft with Solutions Eng.

2025-01-18 Solutions Eng (Elena Park): Feedback - need explicit field for 'can we run a preflight probe inside customer network?' and 'can customer provide snapshot/backup guidance?'. Also recommended 'rollback-method' dropdown (snapshot/revert-config/manual-step).

2025-01-22 PM review: Risk weighting proposal discussed in triage sync. Proposal to add two high-leverage signals: (1) change_window_width_hours (narrow windows add +8 risk), (2) upgrade_script_provenance (internal/supplied/third-party; third-party +10 risk).

2025-01-29 Engineering feedback: Preflight probe MVP feasible but will only cover connectivity and container image availability checks (not execute customer scripts). Auto-run of customer scripts deferred to Q2 due to security gating and isolation work.

2025-02-02 Security review (L. Huang): Security requires that any customer-supplied scripts are executed only inside a customer-managed sandbox with explicit attestations and signed artifacts. Marked security_review_required = true. Recommended HSM/KMS check for any config containing secrets.

2025-02-04 Pilot planning: Identified three candidate customers (Enterprise A, Enterprise B, Partner C) for pilot. Enterprise A prefers weekend windows (UTC+1). Enterprise B has full airgap and provides signed upgrade artifacts. Partner C has narrow 2-hour weekday windows — recommend manual lane.

2025-02-05 Marco Ruiz: Updated PRD with pilot checklist and created GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-onprem-preflight/pull/1842. Slack thread #private-onprem-upgrades contains stakeholder approvals. Next: finalize intake UI changes and schedule pilot runbooks with Ops (target week of 2025-02-17).
notes: Decision log: We will not attempt to auto-execute customer-supplied upgrade scripts in Q1. Focus is on observability (preflight), intake clarity, and operator runbooks.
Trade-offs considered: Full automation reduces ops cost but increases security burden and isolation complexity. Chosen path reduces immediate risk and allows measurable improvements to SLA metrics.
Follow-ups: (1) Ops runbook rehearsal scheduled for 2025-02-18. (2) Security to provide artifact signing checklist by 2025-02-10. (3) UX to implement intake fields in Console by 2025-02-12.
Metrics to track: time-to-schedule (request -> scheduled window), number of escalations during upgrade, operator-hours per upgrade, % of requests eligible for fast-lane.
Historical sample: Reviewed 24 private deploy requests in 2024; 9 had change windows <4 hours and accounted for 67% of weekend oncall disruptions.
